module_title: Norm vs. Criterion-Referenced Tests, HPC & PARAKH (Advanced)
introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced DSSSB/KVS exams, this level dissects the statistical nature of assessments (Norm vs. Criterion), explores the systemic evaluation reforms mandated by NEP 2020 (PARAKH and the 360-degree Holistic Progress Card).

core_concepts.title: Norm-Referenced Test (NRT)
core_concepts.description:
Evaluates a student's performance by COMPARING them to a group of their peers (the 'norm' group).
- Purpose: To rank, sort, and filter students. Produces percentiles.
- Characteristics: Competes student against student. Tells you who is the best, but not necessarily what they learned.
- Examples: Competitive entrance exams (JEE, NEET, CTET percentile ranking), IQ tests.

core_concepts.title: Criterion-Referenced Test (CRT)
core_concepts.description:
Evaluates a student's performance against a pre-defined set of standards, criteria, or learning objectives, regardless of how other students perform.
- Purpose: To determine mastery of a specific skill. Produces percentages.
- Characteristics: Competes student against a standard. All students can theoretically score 100% if they master the skill.
- Examples: Driving test, class spelling test, passing a teaching certification at a 60% threshold.

core_concepts.title: NEP 2020: 360-Degree Holistic Progress Card (HPC)
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 abolishes the traditional report card (which only reflected summative, cognitive marks). 
The new HPC evaluates the student across all three domains: Cognitive, Affective (Socio-Emotional), and Psychomotor (Physical). 
Crucially, it is '360-degree' because it incorporates:
1. Teacher Assessment
2. Self-Assessment (Assessment AS learning)
3. Peer Assessment
4. Parent feedback on home learning.

core_concepts.title: PARAKH (National Assessment Centre)
core_concepts.description:
PARAKH stands for **Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development**. 
- Established by NEP 2020 as a standard-setting body under NCERT. 
- Mandate: To guide all recognized school boards in India to shift their assessment patterns from rote memorization to competency-based, formative evaluation. It conducts national achievement surveys to monitor the health of the education system.

important_entities.name: Assessment IN Learning
important_entities.key_fact: A deep constructivist concept often merged with 'Assessment AS Learning'.
important_entities.significance: While 'As' learning focuses on explicit metacognition (self-assessment), 'IN' learning occurs when an assessment activity ITSELF serves as a learning moment. E.g., An open-book collaborative quiz where students learn new facts *while* trying to find the answers.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners often ask if the CTET exam is Norm-referenced or Criterion-referenced. The CTET is strictly **Criterion-Referenced**. You only need to cross a fixed threshold (90 marks out of 150 / 60%) to pass, regardless of how many other people pass. In contrast, DSSSB/KVS job recruitment exams are **Norm-Referenced** because there are limited seats, and you must outscore others to be selected.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If you are compared to your **N**eighbors (peers), it is a **N**orm-referenced test. If you are compared to a fixed **C**riteria (rule), it is a **C**riterion-referenced test.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks about the primary objective of the new assessment policies under NEP 2020, always look for the keyword **'Holistic Development'** or **'Assessment of Core Competencies'**. Eliminate any option that suggests 'increasing competition' or 'standardizing board exam scores'.
